name: cp-compliance (switching)
description: effective UP/DN switching-time mismatch of the charge pump, at three control-node voltages across the Vctrl window
claim: #9 (design-input claim, not a spec line) -- how far apart are the charge pump's two polarities in TIME? A DC sweep cannot see switching asymmetry, but it is the effective UP/DN pulse-width skew (`w_eff = q / i_ss`) that turns charge-pump asymmetry into static phase error and hence reference spurs. This is the timing half of the same `#9` claim the DC bench (`sim/cp-compliance/testbench`) answers in the current domain; both write into the `sim/cp-compliance/` experiment directory.
methodology: **Timing-mismatch measurement**: two charge-pump instances are pulsed from the SAME control edge, one hardwired UP-active and one DN-active, each into its own control node held at `vctrl` by an ideal source. Sharing the stimulus edge is the point: any measured UP-vs-DN difference is then the pump's own asymmetry, with no stimulus skew mixed in. Per polarity the deck reports `i_ss` (steady state late in the 5 ns pulse), `q` (charge over the whole switching event, INCLUDING the tail-node charge-sharing transient at switch-on) and `w_eff = q / i_ss`, the effective pulse width the loop actually sees. `wskew = w_up - w_dn` is the headline number.

**The measurements are taken in the control block, not as netlist `.measure` cards, and that is load-bearing.** The 50 % turn-on/turn-off delays trigger on a threshold of `i_ss/2` -- half a value that only exists once the transient has run. A netlist-level `.measure ... val='...'` expression is expanded by ngspice's `.param` machinery before the simulation starts and cannot reference a measurement result, so the pre-migration deck computed `iup_h`/`idn_h` with `let` after the `meas` that produced `iup_ss`. This manifest keeps exactly that sequence by putting it in `analyses` (which the harness passes through to `.control` verbatim) and exporting each result through the manifest's `measure` block. `td=` is likewise load-bearing, and is needed on the TARG clause as well as the TRIG clause: ngspice searches each clause independently from t=0 unless told otherwise, so without it the turn-OFF measurements latch onto a crossing belonging to the turn-ON event and report a negative delay.

**One ngspice invocation per (PVT corner, control voltage)** -- 45 x 3 = 135 points, the pre-migration grid unchanged. `vctrl` is a declared `sweeps` axis rather than a run.sh loop variable, taking the two ends and the middle of DR-001 Decision 2's ~0.9-2.4 V window.

The trim code is held at the nominal b1 b0 = 10 (3 unit legs). The trim RANGE is characterized by the DC bench; the switching asymmetry is a property of the shared steering switch and the tail node, which the unit-element trim construction leaves unchanged.

**Bias generation is out of scope and idealized**: the four bias nodes are driven from ideal current sources at 4x the unit-leg current, exactly as in the DC bench and in `sim/devchar-cp`. The skew reported here is therefore the OUTPUT STAGE's own.

Transient: 20 ns at a 5 ps maximum timestep, `reltol` 1e-4 / `abstol` 1e-14. `rshunt = 1e12` resolves the disabled trim legs' floating cascode mid-node (3.3 pA at 3.3 V, below the abstol floor). `itl4 = 200` raises the transient Newton-iteration limit -- a solver-EFFORT knob, not a tolerance: every convergence tolerance is unchanged, so the converged solution is unchanged (verified bit-for-bit at typical/27C/3.30V/Vctrl=1.65V, which converges either way). It is needed because the DR-005 dump-node buffer puts two MOS gates on the control node, and the ideal source holding that node has to carry their displacement current: with everything else in DC steady state that branch current numerically jitters at a few times the 1e-14 A abstol, and ngspice's default 10 iterations are not enough to settle it, so it halves the timestep to nothing at 2 of the 135 points (both at Vctrl = 2.4 V on the 3.63 V supply). Raising abstol instead does NOT fix it and would have loosened a real tolerance.

**Limitation (nominal skew only)**: `sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0`. Everything here is systematic; RANDOM device mismatch is #15's campaign (`mc-cp-mismatch`), and these numbers are what that distribution should be centred on.
**Axes not swept**: passive corner sections (`res_*`, `mimcap_*`, `moscap_*`) N/A -- the DUT is `nfet_03v3`/`pfet_03v3` only (DR-002 Decision 3); it contains no resistors or capacitors.

**Cross-record comparability (simulator / host delta)**: the pre-migration records this campaign supersedes (`20260731-091153-7d78a47`, `20260731-122451-63e4b47`, `20260731-194124-afa338c`) were taken with **ngspice-46 on Darwin 25.6.0 / arm64**; harness runs on this project's Linux host use **ngspice-42 on Linux x86_64**. The record's own Environment provenance field states the simulator and host of THIS run and is authoritative for it -- this bullet exists so the delta against the superseded record is never left implicit.

x.description: vctrl -- the control-node voltage the switching event is measured at: the two edges and the middle of DR-001 Decision 2's ~0.9-2.4 V Vctrl window

x0.9.description: low edge of the Vctrl window

x2.4.description: high edge of the Vctrl window

analyses: meas tran iup_ss avg i(vou) from=14n to=15n
meas tran idn_ss avg i(vod) from=14n to=15n
meas tran qup integ i(vou) from=9.5n to=15n
meas tran qdn integ i(vod) from=9.5n to=15n
meas tran ton_up trig v(ctl) val=$&vmid rise=1 td=9n targ i(vou) val=$&iup_h rise=1 td=9n
meas tran ton_dn trig v(ctl) val=$&vmid rise=1 td=9n targ i(vod) val=$&idn_h fall=1 td=9n
meas tran toff_up trig v(ctl) val=$&vmid fall=1 td=15n targ i(vou) val=$&iup_h fall=1 td=15n
meas tran toff_dn trig v(ctl) val=$&vmid fall=1 td=15n targ i(vod) val=$&idn_h rise=1 td=15n

effective pulse width (the headline).description: q / i_ss per polarity -- the effective width the loop sees, including the tail-node charge-sharing transient -- and the UP-vs-DN difference that turns pump asymmetry into static phase error

steady state and delivered charge.description: the DC value each switch eventually delivers, and the charge integrated over the whole switching event

edge delays (diagnostics).description: 50 %-of-i_ss crossings referenced to the 50 % control edge; reported for context -- the headline skew above is derived from integrated charge and needs no edge search
